linked_urls.summary: Adam is Interim Director of the UK’s AI Security Institute ( AISI ), a world-leading government organisation dedicated to understanding and mitigating the security risks posed by artificial intelligence. He was previously a senior national security leader and GCHQ’s Chief AI Officer, specialising in managing AI risks and opportunities. He oversaw strategic initiatives to understand AI threats, enhance security, and accelerate responsible AI adoption across the community. Adam’s experience includes leading a cutting-edge AI research lab, fostering public-private partnerships to tackle key security challenges and crisis leadership during major terrorist incidents. He has also advised on security and defence policy in both Whitehall and Washington.

Quoting @jrosseruk
Introducing ✨Infusion✨, our *new paper* made possible by the UK AISI Challenge Fund and Sovereign AI!
1/8🧵 TL;DR
Influence functions are commonly used to attribute model behavior to its training data. In this paper we explored the reverse: whether it's possible to use influence functions to craft training data that induces model behavior?
Huge thank you to my amazing collaborators for making this possible
@LauraRuis @_robertkirk @egrefen @j_foerst and of course

clean_title: AI systems disclose their identity when asked? Introducing the RealityTest benchmark
summary:
Do AI systems disclose their identity when asked?
In our new paper, we present the RealityTest benchmark, which comprehensively tests whether AI systems disclose their identity when asked - grounded in human data on how people encounter and question AI in the real world.
📷 https://pbs.twimg.com/media/HKSulKRW4AAfM6B.png
